name: Restaurants
one_liner: Quick-service, fast-casual, and full-service dining operators whose economics are set by unit-level volumes, food and labor costs, and whether the brand owns or franchises its locations.
how_it_makes_money: Company-operated restaurants earn the spread between menu prices and food, labor, and occupancy costs. Franchisors earn royalties (a percentage of franchisee sales), upfront fees, and sometimes rent, giving them asset-light, high-margin revenue streams.
revenue_formula: Revenue = number of units × average unit volume (AUV)
AUV = transactions per day × average check × operating days
Franchisor revenue = system-wide sales × royalty rate + franchise fees + rent
cost_structure: Food and packaging: commonly roughly 25-35% of sales
Labor: similar in size to food cost, rising with minimum wage increases
Occupancy: rent and utilities, largely fixed
Third-party delivery commissions for off-premise orders
Marketing, including franchise ad fund contributions
margins: Restaurant-level margins are often roughly 15-20% for strong operators, while corporate operating margins for heavily franchised brands can be far higher because they collect royalties without running stores. Menu pricing power, traffic, labor efficiency, and franchise mix drive the spread.

key_metrics.name: Same-store sales (SSS)
key_metrics.what: Sales growth in existing restaurants, split into traffic and average check.

key_metrics.name: Average unit volume (AUV)
key_metrics.what: Annual sales per restaurant, a key indicator of brand strength and unit economics.

key_metrics.name: Restaurant-level margin
key_metrics.what: Profit at the four walls after food, labor, and occupancy.

key_metrics.name: Prime cost
key_metrics.what: Food plus labor as a share of sales, the main controllable cost lever.

key_metrics.name: Cash-on-cash return / payback
key_metrics.what: Return on new-unit build cost, used to decide expansion pace.

key_metrics.name: Digital mix
key_metrics.what: Share of sales through apps, kiosks, and delivery, linked to loyalty and data.

trends: Value wars as quick-service chains discount to win back lower-income traffic after menu price increases
Drive-thru and digital ordering growth, with smaller-format and pickup-focused stores
Loyalty programs and app-based personalization driving frequency
Labor cost pressure from state and city minimum wage laws, especially in California
Kitchen automation and AI voice ordering at drive-thrus
Fast-casual brands expanding rapidly while casual dining consolidates
